summary: Georg Forster worked in Indology and other fields after studying at Saint Peter's School. He held posts at Vilnius University (1784–1787) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (circa 1788–1793).

Georg Friedrich Grotefend worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at Lessing-Gymnasium and the University of Göttingen (circa 1795–1797).

Georg Huth specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Leipzig (circa 1885–1889), he held a post at the University of Berlin (circa 1892–1906).

Georg Kaibel was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Rostock (circa 1879–1882), University of Breslau (circa 1882–1883), University of Greifswald (circa 1883–1886), and University of Göttingen (circa 1897–1901).

Georg Ludolf Dissen worked in linguistics and other fields. After studying at the University of Göttingen (circa 1803–1807), he held academic posts at the University of Marburg (circa 1812–1813) and the University of Göttingen (circa 1813–1837).

Georg Martin Dursch studied at the University of Tübingen (1819–1824) and the University of Paris under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (circa 1827–1829). Working in Indology and religious studies, he became a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen in 1829.

Georg Morgenstierne studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Wilhelm Schulze, and Sten Konow. Working in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held professorships at the University of Gothenburg and University of Oslo.
Georg Simmel worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at the University of Berlin (circa 1876–1881), he held a post there from circa 1885 to 1914.

Georg Wilhelm Freytag studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. A scholar of linguistics and other fields, he held positions at Göttingen, the University of Königsberg, and as professor of oriental languages at Bonn.

Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, Tübinger Stift, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Jena under Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling. He held academic posts at Jena, Heidelberg, and Berlin.

Georg von Simson studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Göttingen. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he served as an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and later as professor at the University of Oslo.

Georg von der Gabelentz studied at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. Working in Sinology, linguistics, and Japanology, he served as professor at the University of Leipzig, professor at the University of Berlin, and member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

George A. Kennedy studied Sinology and linguistics at the University of Berlin under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke (circa 1932–1934). He subsequently held a post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

George A. Keyworth studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA under Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, Shuizhao Wang, and Robert Buswell. Active in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at the University of Colorado and University of Saskatchewan.

George Abraham Grierson studied at St Bees School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College Dublin. Working in linguistics and Indology, he served in the Indian Civil Service, as Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India, and Governor of SOAS.
George Adolphus Jacob worked in Indology. His career included service as a colonel in the Bombay Staff Corps and the Indian Army, as well as a fellowship at the University of Mumbai.

George Baumann studied at the University of Heidelberg and the Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen. Working in Indology, he held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Bibliotheksreferendar at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001.

George Cardona studied at NYU, Yale under Paul Thieme and Warren Cowgill, and in India with traditional scholars. A specialist in Indology and linguistics, he was a long-time professor at the University of Pennsylvania and fellow at CASBS.

George Chemparathy studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. Specializing in Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and as a professor at Utrecht University from circa 1975 to 1993.

George Cowgill was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Stanford University (circa 1948–1952) and Harvard University (circa 1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (circa 1960–1990) and Arizona State University (circa 1990–2018).
